title: Harness selection and execution
intro: Views of the harness-dispatch command and of Grove's use of it, matching the area specification's package, execution, supervision, Grove-integration and original-creator topics. These are source-package and process views, not deployment containers; the state view is a reading aid, not a checked model. Graphs begin at a dark Start here node with numbered steps; sequence views begin at the first message, the state view at its initial state.

groups.title: Package boundary
groups.description: One public command, an installed private worker, one owner policy, optional caller adapters, and the domain-free runner both sides use.

groups.title: Execution and supervision
groups.description: Selection ends before the harness starts; dispatch then stays its parent to the end, catches its exit signal and reports how the run ended.

groups.title: Grove integration
groups.description: Grove launches through run with no parameter, gives the session a launch directory, records a teardown itself and reads the loop's next step from the run ending.

groups.title: Original creator and review
groups.description: A review carries a reference to its creator's run; run records outlive the task tree.

discussion.title: harness-dispatch supervises the harness; Grove keeps the leaf, the prompt and the teardown record
discussion.status: Proposed in harness-wrapper-k2; reviewed in harness-wrapper-k3, whose findings harness-wrapper-k5 integrated before planning
discussion.summary: run spawns the harness as its own job and stays its parent: it catches the exit signal (harness-dispatch exit, carrying nothing), escalates, restores the terminal, confines when asked, appends its end observation and writes the run ending to the caller's ending file. Grove passes no parameter, names its launch directory as the exit directory, records a teardown with grove-llm record-teardown, and reads teardown, exit signal or anything else as finished, relaunch or stopped.

updatedDiagrams.summary: New: the two nested jobs from the shell to the harness, who holds the terminal while selecting and while running, and where the exit signal goes, and how a launcher takes the terminal back, a dead dispatch's included.
New: a supervised run's states from selection to its run ending, with the escalation and cancellation paths and the group cleanup before the ending is reported.
New: how the driver reads a reaped launch as interrupted, finished, relaunched or stopped.
Both launches go through run: the lifecycle launch passes no parameter and names its launch directory; grove run passes --confine and publishes on the exit-signal ending.
The front spawns and supervises the harness instead of replacing itself, and records the end.
Added the shared runner, the exit signal back to dispatch and the run ending back to the caller.
Dispatch spawns the producer and the reviewer rather than exec'ing them.

diagrams.title: Caller, dispatcher and policy packages
diagrams.caption: Source packages and runtime participants. The command holds no catalog: the owner's function returns the command. Grove-specific relationship parsing belongs to the optional adapter. keyed-launch has no Grove, task-tree or jj dependency; dispatch runs the harness through it and Grove runs dispatch through it.

diagrams.title: Prepare, record and supervise the harness
diagrams.caption: The worker shares the front's job and has null stdin, and is reaped before the harness starts. Cancellation or timeout before the handoff launches nothing; a signal after it cancels the run, which dispatch ends and records. Keeping a deciding agent from executing the task it evaluates is its policy owner's job.

diagrams.title: Two nested jobs: driver, dispatch, harness
diagrams.caption: Each supervisor makes its own child a foreground job, as a shell would. While the policy selects the terminal is dispatch's group's; while the harness runs it is the harness's group's alone, so a typed Ctrl-C reaches only the harness. The driver sets GROVE_LAUNCH_DIR for dispatch; dispatch sets HARNESS_DISPATCH_EXIT_FILE for the harness, and the exit verb creates that file. The escalation is grace, TERM, kill-grace, KILL on group H, ending its descendants with it, and whatever ends the harness, what remains of group H is killed before the harness is reaped. Each launcher takes the terminal back from its child's group with the attributes it saved restored, and, when its child died of a signal, from whichever group holds it but its own or the session leader's, so a dispatch that died still leaves the driver a terminal to restore.

diagrams.title: A supervised run from selection to its ending
diagrams.caption: Grace 2 s and kill-grace 5 s are dispatch's constants. A confined run is killed at once on cancellation. When the harness exits, what remains of its group is killed before the reap, and the ending is reported only once the group is gone; a group still present is a supervision failure, with no ending file. A run that started no harness has no ending. A dispatch killed by SIGKILL leaves the harness orphaned and its attempt as it stood; that path has no state here because nothing in dispatch runs it.

diagrams.title: Grove's two launches: lifecycle and confined standalone
diagrams.caption: Grove passes no parameter and reads no configuration. The two run-mechanics flags reach no policy. A lifecycle session ends with harness-dispatch exit, after grove-llm record-teardown when it tore the grove down. A standalone invocation is selected outside the sandbox and confined by dispatch, gets a run record, and publishes only on the exit-signal ending with exit 0.

diagrams.title: How the driver reads a reaped launch
diagrams.caption: A teardown record finishes whatever the run ending, so a finish session whose harness exits on its own after recording still finishes. Only the exit signal relaunches, so a harness orphaned by dispatch's death is never joined by a second session on the same tree.

diagrams.title: Where each option keeps the creator's provider
diagrams.caption: The decision is A. A lookup keyed by handle must tell this grove's handle from an earlier grove's in the same workspace, which needs durable state Grove deliberately lacks (B). A globally unique run reference carried by the review needs none (A).

diagrams.title: Producer names its run; the review resolves it
diagrams.caption: The run reference is written by the session that ran under it, so the provider comes from dispatch's immutable record rather than a transcription. The association itself is that session's attestation, not verified. A session that finishes without a run removes any earlier line, and the owner declares the finished artifact's provider.

diagrams.title: Resolve the Creator line before selecting a reviewer
diagrams.caption: The supplied example policy. Every invocation and retry takes the same path; a retry reads the same line and the same immutable run, so it cannot change the creator.
